def factor_vol_regime_price_impact(df):
    """Conditional illiquidity: difference in average absolute returns between high-volume and low-volume days."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    abs_ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change().abs()
    is_high_vol, is_low_vol, _ = alpha_tools.classify_volume_regime(df_copy["volume"], window=20)
    high_sum = (abs_ret * is_high_vol).rolling(20, min_periods=1).sum()
    high_cnt = is_high_vol.rolling(20, min_periods=1).sum()
    low_sum = (abs_ret * is_low_vol).rolling(20, min_periods=1).sum()
    low_cnt = is_low_vol.rolling(20, min_periods=1).sum()
    avg_high = (high_sum / high_cnt.replace(0, np.nan)).fillna(0.0)
    avg_low = (low_sum / low_cnt.replace(0, np.nan)).fillna(0.0)
    factor = avg_high - avg_low
    df_copy["factor_vol_regime_price_impact"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_vol_regime_price_impact"]
description: Measures conditional price impact by contrasting absolute returns on high-volume vs low-volume days. A positive spread indicates high-volume days produce larger price moves relative to low-volume days, suggesting liquidity stress. A negative spread suggests volume efficiently absorbs order flow. This is a novel mechanism not captured by continuous Amihud ratios or asymmetric volatility. Windows with no high/low volume observations are treated as zero contribution.
